title: P0 — Go module, Fiber v3 API, SQLite store, rig compat probe
body:
## Context

The service does not exist yet. This issue creates the skeleton every later issue builds on. Design: `design.md`
§5 (architecture), §6 (data), §7 (rig contract). Tasks: `tasks.md` 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.6.

## Scope

- Go module `github.com/dinhtrung/fleet-console`, Go 1.25, package layout `cmd/fleet-console`,
  `internal/{store,forge,rig,git,decide,act,web}`.
- Fiber v3 app with `/api/health`, `/api/compat`, bearer middleware, `Idempotency-Key` middleware, graceful shutdown.
- SQLite via `modernc.org/sqlite`: WAL, `busy_timeout`, migrations, single-writer guard. Schema exactly as design §6 —
  **no `queue_row`, `decision`, `lease` or `task` tables**.
- Rig compat probe: `rig --version` floor, one real `queue list -A -a --json` and `ps --nodes --full --json` read,
  required-field checks (missing `state`, `pickup_state`, `destination_session`, seat identity = error), unknown
  keys logged once, `GET /api/compat` exposes the result.

## Acceptance

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` all exit 0.
- `go test ./...` green, including: store create/reopen/migrate; 401 without token and 200 with; repeated
  `Idempotency-Key` returns the first `event_id`; compat probe passes on a fixture and fails naming the field when
  `pickup_state` is renamed.
- `fleet-console --compat` prints observed rig version, floor and both parsed shapes.

## Evidence in the PR

Paste the four commands and their real output. State the rig version on the fleet box.

## Constraints

Do not implement the mirror, decide or act loops here. Do not add a web UI. Fiber v3 only — no `net/http` handlers
except the health fallback if Fiber cannot serve it.

title: P0 — Port the dispatcher rules and build the golden oracle
body:
## Context

`~/bin/fleet-autodispatch.py` (1534 lines) is the proven contract. The port must be provable, not plausible. Tasks
`tasks.md` 1.4, 1.5; invariants `design.md` §2 and §9.

## Scope

- Pure functions over a snapshot: epic skip, parent gate, `onhold` cascade, live-row-body idempotency, branch on
  origin with no merged CR, one-way blocking (GitLab smaller-number rule / GitHub native `blocked_by`), ascending
  order, cap by free builders.
- Every skip produces a **reason string**; a candidate with no reason is a test failure.
- Oracle harness: run the Python dispatcher in dry-run and the Go plan on the same recorded inputs; diff task sets
  and reasons. Record at least 20 real ticks under `internal/decide/testdata/ticks/`.

## Acceptance

- One table test per rule, named after the rule.
- `go test ./internal/decide -run TestOracle` green over the recorded ticks.
- Killing the forge read yields `stale`, not "no tasks".

## Evidence in the PR

The oracle diff (empty), the tick count, and one tick's input/output pair.

## Constraints

Do not "improve" a rule. If a rule looks wrong, implement it as written and open an issue with the data.

title: P0 — Rig adapter and generated rig lifecycle
body:
## Context

The app must never have a hand-authored rig, and must survive rig `--json` drift. Tasks `tasks.md` 2.1–2.6; design
§7 and §12; delta `specs/rig-lifecycle/`.

## Scope

- `internal/rig`: one adapter function per CLI command (`QueueList`, `QueueShow`, `QueueCreate`, `QueueUpdate`,
  `QueueHandoff`, `QueueResolve`, `Seats`, `Parked`, `ProviderSignals`, `SpecValidate`, `Up`, `Plan`, `Down`,
  `Grow`, `Export`, `Launch`, `Send`), domain types out, no `map[string]any` across the boundary.
- Spec template + renderer: rig name, per-seat cwd/runtime/model, account env, builder count, guidance, culture.
- Launch: write spec dir → `rig spec validate` → `rig specs sync` → `rig up --plan` → `rig up --non-interruptive` →
  verify every seat `running`.
- Growth with `rig grow` then `rig export` write-back. Teardown `rig down --delete` + archive; refuse with live rows.
- Seat seeding before launch: provider key in `state/omp/<seat>/agent/config.yml`, `mcp.json` with the project's
  serena entry; never print the key.

## Acceptance

- `go test ./internal/rig` green over recorded fixtures for each command.
- One real throwaway rig launched and removed on the fleet box, with both JSON outputs in the PR.
- A spec rendered from a project row validates and launches 3 seats; deleting a seat's credential makes the launch
  refuse naming the file.

## Evidence in the PR

The rendered spec, `rig spec validate --json`, the plan, `rig ps --nodes --json`, and the teardown result.

## Constraints

Never `rig archive` (it keeps the name). Never edit `~/.openrig/specs` by hand outside the renderer.

title: P1 — Forge adapters: GitHub first, GitLab parity
body:
## Context

The rig does not read the forge. This is the app's reason to exist. Tasks `tasks.md` 3.1–3.5; design §8; delta
`specs/forge/`.

## Scope

- Interface `Item` / `ChangeRequest` / `Check` + exactly four writes (marker label, comment, close item, merge at sha).
- GitHub: issues, sub-issues for the epic relation, issue dependencies (`blocked_by`), PRs, check runs and commit
  statuses, `gh pr merge --squash --match-head-commit <sha>`.
- GitLab: `glab api` items with `related_items` (smaller-number rule), MRs, head pipeline jobs with `allow_failure`,
  `glab mr merge --sha`.
- Auth from the CLI's own store only. Bounded per-tick request budget; 401/5xx surfaces as project `stale`.

## Acceptance

- Fixture tests per adapter from recorded payloads of `dinhtrung/fleet-console` (GitHub) and `traffic-simulator-v2`
  (GitLab).
- The same decide test passes with both adapters.
- A failing check marked allow-failure does not read red; a docs-only PR with no checks reads green with the reason.

## Evidence in the PR

Fixture file names, the two decide runs, and one real `gh api` read.

## Constraints

No forge token in config, DB or events. No GraphQL unless REST cannot answer (record why).

title: P1 — Mirror loop and decide pass in dry-run
body:
## Context

Mirror is read-only; decide is pure and replayable. Tasks `tasks.md` 4.1–4.6; design §5 and §9.

## Scope

- Mirror: items + links + PR/MR + checks, rig queue/seat snapshot, `git ls-remote` branch index, per-project stamps
  and `stale`.
- Decide: intents only (`dispatch`, `nudge`, `clear_marker`, `close_epic`, `raise_decision`), no writes.
- Housekeeping before the "no free builder" early return: prune, reset stalled (≤3), marker reconcile, re-nudge
  (15 min / 30 min cooldown), epic close.
- Incident detectors: parked (open CR, no verdict, no live row) and marker leak (merged CR, item open).
- One week of dry-run compared with the live dispatcher (task 4.6) — start it, report the diff count.

## Acceptance

- Killing the forge CLI leaves the last sync time and `stale: true`, never an empty board.
- One test per housekeeping pass asserting the events it would write.
- Incident fixtures produce the exact question text.
- `docs/cutover.md` records the dry-run comparison.

## Evidence in the PR

Test names, a stale-state response, the two incident questions, and the first dry-run tick.

title: P2 — Act loop: dispatch, verdict capture, merge watchdog
body:
## Context

The only place that mutates the world. Tasks `tasks.md` 5.1–5.5; design §10–§11.

## Scope

- Dispatch: fetch → base sha → worktree add-or-reuse → brief → `rig queue create --source human@kernel
  --destination <seat> --body-file` → marker label → dispatch row. Second run must be a no-op naming the row.
- Row actions: resolve, handoff, close-as-superseded, re-nudge — one rig call + one event each.
- Verdict capture: newest note wins, `accept|reject`, sha must match that note's sha.
- Merge watchdog: four facts re-read in the act pass (verdict sha = head, checks green with allow-failure, mergeable,
  body closes the item). Refusal names the missing fact.
- Post-merge: verify the item closed, close it on `Refs`, clear marker, unblock next.

## Acceptance

- Four refusal tests and one end-to-end merge on a docs-only PR.
- A `Refs #n` body ends with the item closed and an event naming the reason.
- Re-running a dispatch intent creates no second worktree or row.

## Evidence in the PR

The four refusal outputs, the merge call with `--match-head-commit`, and the event trail of one full item.

title: P3 — Web foundation: shadcn/ui + sage only
body:
## Context

The web scaffold is inherited (React 19, Vite, TanStack Router/Query, Tailwind v4) with five appearances and its own
primitives. The owner chose one library and one appearance. Tasks `tasks.md` 6.1–6.4; deltas `console-ui`.

## Scope

- `npx shadcn@latest init` on the existing Vite app: `components.json`, `@` alias, Base UI primitives,
  `tw-animate-css`, `cva`/`clsx`/`tailwind-merge`. Pin versions in `package.json`.
- Delete the light, dark, dusk and ember token blocks from `src/index.css`, their entries in
  `src/lib/appearance.ts`, the `dark` custom variant, the appearance switcher and its shell usage. `:root` carries
  sage. A stale `localStorage` value must render sage and be cleared.
- Token bridge: map `--background/--foreground/--primary/--border/--ring/--radius` onto the sage roles.
- Replace Button, Dialog, Menu, Field, Toast with shadcn versions and delete the replaced files; update every import.

## Acceptance

- `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build` exit 0.
- `grep -rn 'data-theme="\(light\|dark\|dusk\|ember\)"' src index.html` returns nothing.
- No palette hex in `src/components/ui`; colours resolve through bridge variables.
- One screenshot of the surviving shell on sage, and one shadcn Dialog open.

## Evidence in the PR

The grep outputs, the build log, and the two screenshots.

## Constraints

Do not restyle screens beyond swapping primitives. Do not keep a second appearance "for later". Keep the ruled,
no-elevation layout rules from `DESIGN.md`.

title: P3 — Board, decisions, seats, task drawer on the new foundation
body:
## Context

Once the foundation is shadcn+sage, the product surface is built on it. Tasks `tasks.md` 6.5–6.6; delta
`console-ui`; API design §14.

## Scope

- Embedded SPA (`go:embed dist`), SPA fallback, SSE `/api/stream`.
- Board: projects, counts, items ordered by number, and the **reason** each item is not moving.
- Decisions: read from the rig (queue rows to a person), oldest first, deadline badge, options, free-text; answering
  posts `POST /api/decisions/{id}/answer` → `rig queue resolve`.
- Seats: state, observed model, permission mode, last activity, read-only pane tail.
- Task drawer: brief, branch, worktree, PR, checks, verdict, events.

## Acceptance

- `go build` serves the board with no Node at runtime; `curl -N /api/stream` prints one event on a state change.
- One screenshot per screen: two projects (one paused, one with a parked decision), a real omp seat, a merged item's
  drawer.
- Answering a fixture decision writes `rig queue resolve` and one event, and the row leaves the queue.

## Evidence in the PR

The four screenshots, the SSE line, and the event row written by the answer.

title: P4 — Alerts, quota, second project, cutover
body:
## Context

Last phase: the loop must run unattended and the old dispatcher must be retired without a double dispatch. Tasks
`tasks.md` 7.1–7.4.

## Scope

- Telegram escalation on deadline breach and on quota: one message per decision, edited not repeated, deep link.
- Quota: two seats stalled within 5 minutes → one decision, pause dispatch to that rig; source `rig provider signals`.
- Second project with its own generated rig and isolated capacity.
- Cutover: import dispatcher state, disable the old timer, run one item end-to-end, update `docs/my-stack.md`.

## Acceptance

- Forced breach sends exactly one message with project, item, question, link.
- Two projects dispatch without a shared worktree or number collision.
- One full item: dispatched → reviewed → merged → epic closed; board empty with a reason per closed item.
- `docs/my-stack.md` names the binary, unit, port and kill switch.

## Evidence in the PR

The Telegram message id (not its content), the two-project board screenshot, and the cutover transcript.

title: P0 — Stack provisioning and single-binary packaging
body:
## Context

A new box must reach a working stack without a human reciting the steps. Change set `stack-provisioning` (all tasks
1.1–7.1). This issue is independent of the service code except for `--compat` and `--version`.

## Scope

- `stack.lock` (runtime, rig, harness, forge, tooling, app + sha256) and preflight (OS/arch, sudo, disk, ports,
  existing versions).
- `install.sh`: dry-run default, `--apply`, `--profile fleet|app`, `--verify`, `--upgrade`; vendor installers with
  checksums; marker blocks and dated backups for every config edit; four human stops exiting `3`.
- Verify gate: versions vs lock, `rig doctor` with exactly the two expected findings, daemon running, one real forge
  read, `fleet-console --compat` 0, `/api/health` 200, units active+enabled, linger on.
- Packaging: `Makefile` (`web`, `build` with `CGO_ENABLED=0` + `-trimpath` + embed + tzdata, `release` tar+sha256),
  `--version --json`, host-tool check at boot, optional multi-stage `Dockerfile` with declared mounts, reversible
  upgrade with DB backup.
- `docs/install.md`.

## Acceptance

- `./install.sh --dry-run` writes nothing and prints every pin.
- A second `--apply` reports every step `already satisfied` and the tree is unchanged.
- On a complete box `--verify` prints ok for every check and exits 0; deleting one tool fails exactly its check.
- `make build` produces one file that serves the board with no `dist/` beside it.
- A forced failed upgrade restores the previous binary.

## Evidence in the PR

The dry-run output, the second-run diff, the verify transcript, `file` on the binary, and the upgrade rollback log.

## Constraints

Do not bundle rig/gh/glab into the default deployment. The Docker image is documented as the exception, with the
host mounts it needs.
